Entry TN-2019-014
OL: 12 Mar 2019 | TL: 14 Mar 2019 | Translated for: Range Officer, Mudumalai (Mudumalay in some older letters)
Letter from: Village Forest Committee Secretary, Gundatti

- "ಹೊಲ" (hola) – I have translated as "enclosure" rather than "field" because the context is about a fenced plot near the elephant corridor. The committee secretary uses it for a plot that has been left fallow for two seasons. [RO: fine, keep enclosure.]
- "ಮಳೆ ಕಾಲ" (male kala) – rainy season; in this letter it refers specifically to the period June–August, not the full monsoon. I noted this in the margin of the translation.
- Place name: "ಬೆಟ್ಟದ ಹಳ್ಳ" (Bettada Halla) – I have kept as "Bettada Halla" with a footnote that the same stream is called "Bettahalla" in the 2017 survey map. Not resolved.
- The secretary's closing phrase "ನಿಮ್ಮ ಕೈಲಿ" (nimma kaili) literally "in your hand" – I rendered it as "at your disposal" because the literal sounds odd in English for a formal letter. This phrase appears often in these letters and I have used the same rendering consistently since Jan 2019.

Ambiguity: The secretary wrote "ಸುಮಾರು 20 ಎಕರೆ" (about 20 acres) but the figure is overwritten and could be 30. I have flagged this in the translation with [?]. Awaiting confirmation from the Range Office before final issue.

Entry TN-2019-027
OL: 2 Jun 2019 | TL: 5 Jun 2019 | Translated for: Assistant Conservator of Forests, Gudalur
Letter from: Field Assistant, Kargudi range

Translator Nair's notes confirm she translates_from_language Kannada. Record status: current.

- This letter arrived with heavy water damage; the top right corner of page 1 is illegible. The date is taken from the postmark. The Field Assistant's name is partially smudged; I have left the name blank in the translation and noted "illegible due to rain damage."
- "ಉರಿ" (uri) – in this context, "burning" or "fire line." The writer uses it to refer to the controlled burn line along the eastern boundary. I translated as "fire line" with a note that the term is local usage; elsewhere in WGCI files it appears as "firebreak."
- The letter mentions "ಕಾಡು ಹಂದಿ" (kadu handi) – wild pig. The writer says the animals have damaged the newly planted saplings near the stream. I have translated as "wild pig" and added a note that the writer might mean "boar" but the term is generic in this letter.
- Place name: "ಮುಡುಮಲೈ" (Mudumalai) spelled as "Mudumalai" in the original; this matches the standard spelling used by the Forest Department, but I have seen "Mudumalay" in older letters from this same Field Assistant. I have kept "Mudumalai" here and noted the variant for the file.

Query: The writer uses "ನಮ್ಮ ಕಡೆ" (namma kade) – literally "our side." I translated as "in our area" but it could also mean "on our side of the boundary." I have flagged this for the officer; the meaning affects whether the fire line is inside or outside the WGCI project area.

Entry TN-2019-014
OL: 12 Mar 2019 | TL: 14 Mar 2019 | Translated for: Range Officer, Mudumalai (Mudumalay in some older letters)
Letter from: Village Forest Committee Secretary, Gundatti

- "ಹೊಲ" (hola) – I have translated as "enclosure" rather than "field" because the context is about a fenced plot near the elephant corridor. The committee secretary uses it for a plot that has been left fallow for two seasons. [RO: fine, keep enclosure.]
- "ಮಳೆ ಕಾಲ" (male kala) – rainy season; in this letter it refers specifically to the period June–August, not the full monsoon. I noted this in the margin of the translation.
- Place name: "ಬೆಟ್ಟದ ಹಳ್ಳ" (Bettada Halla) – I have kept as "Bettada Halla" with a footnote that the same stream is called "Bettahalla" in the 2017 survey map. Not resolved.
- The secretary's closing phrase "ನಿಮ್ಮ ಕೈಲಿ" (nimma kaili) literally "in your hand" – I rendered it as "at your disposal" because the literal sounds odd in English for a formal letter. This phrase appears often in these letters and I have used the same rendering consistently since Jan 2019.

Ambiguity: The secretary wrote "ಸುಮಾರು 20 ಎಕರೆ" (about 20 acres) but the figure is overwritten and could be 30. I have flagged this in the translation with [?]. Awaiting confirmation from the Range Office before final issue.

---

Entry TN-2019-027
OL: 2 Jun 2019 | TL: 5 Jun 2019 | Translated for: Assistant Conservator of Forests, Gudalur
Letter from: Field Assistant, Kargudi range

Translator Nair's notes confirm she translates_from_language Kannada. Record status: current.

- This letter arrived with heavy water damage; the top right corner of page 1 is illegible. The date is taken from the postmark. The Field Assistant's name is partially smudged; I have left the name blank in the translation and noted "illegible due to rain damage."
- "ಉರಿ" (uri) – in this context, "burning" or "fire line." The writer uses it to refer to the controlled burn line along the eastern boundary. I translated as "fire line" with a note that the term is local usage; elsewhere in WGCI files it appears as "firebreak."
- The letter mentions "ಕಾಡು ಹಂದಿ" (kadu handi) – wild pig. The writer says the animals have damaged the newly planted saplings near the stream. I have translated as "wild pig" and added a note that the writer might mean "boar" but the term is generic in this letter.
- Place name: "ಮುಡುಮಲೈ" (Mudumalai) spelled as "Mudumalai" in the original; this matches the standard spelling used by the Forest Department, but I have seen "Mudumalay" in older letters from this same Field Assistant. I have kept "Mudumalai" here and noted the variant for the file.

Query: The writer uses "ನಮ್ಮ ಕಡೆ" (namma kade) – literally "our side." I translated as "in our area" but it could also mean "on our side of the boundary." I have flagged this for the officer; the meaning affects whether the fire line is inside or outside the WGCI project area.

---

Entry TN-2019-041
OL: 18 Aug 2019 | TL: 21 Aug 2019 | Translated for: Project Director, WGCI
Letter from: Village Panchayat Secretary, Bokkapuram (spelled "Bokkapuram" in the original; also seen as "Bokapuram" in some correspondence)

- "ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಜಮೀನು" (sarkari jaminu) – government land. Translated as "government land" with a note that the writer uses this to mean revenue land not yet assigned to any department. Not the same as "forest land" (ಅರಣ್ಯ ಭೂಮಿ, aranya bhoomi) which appears later in the letter.
- The secretary's request uses the phrase "ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು" (dayavittu) – "please" or "kindly." I have used "kindly" in the translation to match the formal register of the original. This is consistent with my earlier translations for this panchayat.
- Place name: "ಬೊಕ್ಕಪುರಂ" (Bokkapuram) – I have kept the spelling as in the original. The same village appears as "Bokkapuram" in the 2018 WGCI annual report and as "Bokapuram" in a 2017 letter from the same secretary. I have not corrected either spelling; I note both variants in the margin.
- The letter includes a list of 14 names (village committee members). The list is handwritten and the last two names are difficult to read. I have typed the first 12 and left the last two as [?] with a note that the original is smudged. I will ask the secretary for confirmation.

- "ಉಪ-ನಿರೀಕ್ಷಕ" (upa-nirikshaka) – literally "sub-inspector." In the forest context here, this is the Deputy Range Forest Officer. - Place name: "ಗುಡ್ಡಲೂರು" (Guddaluru) – the writer spells it with two 'd's. Standard spelling in WGCI records is "Gudalur." I have kept "Gudalur" in the translation and noted the variant in the margin. This is the same village as "Guddalur" in the 2016 boundary survey.
- The letter mentions a fire line "near the 3rd mile" (ಮೂರನೇ ಮೈಲಿ, moorane maili). I have kept "3rd mile" because the distance marker on the road is still called that locally, even though the road is now numbered SH-17. The officer will know which stretch is meant.

Query: The phrase "ಕಳೆದ ವರ್ಷ" (kaleda varsha) – "last year." The letter is dated 26 Aug 2019, so I have translated as "in 2018" rather than "last year" to avoid confusion in the file. **ARTICLE 2: OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE**

2.1 The primary objective of this Agreement is to secure the functional connectivity of the Singara–Kurichi elephant corridor through:

(a) Installation and maintenance of 12 km of solar-powered electric fencing along the village interface zones;

(b) Development of a community-based early warning system for elephant movements;

(c) Restoration of 25 hectares of degraded forest patches within the corridor;

(d) Capacity building of 60 local youth as village-level conservation volunteers;

(e) Regular monitoring and documentation of elephant movement patterns using camera traps and GPS collars.

2.2 The Parties shall jointly prepare a detailed Annual Work Plan and Budget, which shall be submitted to the Steering Committee for approval no later than 30 days before the start of each program year.

2.3 Any change to the scope of work shall require the written consent of both Parties, to be recorded as an amendment to this Agreement.

**ARTICLE 3: TERM AND TERMINATION**

3.1 This Agreement shall be effective from the Effective Date and shall remain in force for a period of three (3) years, unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Article (the "Initial Term").

3.2 The Agreement may be renewed for subsequent periods by mutual written consent of the Parties, with the terms of such renewal to be negotiated in good faith and recorded in a renewal addendum.

The partnership agreement records WGCI's registration_number as NGO/2015/00482. Record status: current.

3.3 Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon ninety (90) days' written notice to the other Party, provided that such termination shall not affect the obligations already incurred prior to the date of termination.

3.4 In the event of termination, the Parties shall jointly prepare a handover plan for ongoing activities, assets, and data, and shall settle all financial matters within sixty (60) days of the termination date.

**ARTICLE 4: FINANCIAL ARRANGEMENTS**

4.1 WTI shall provide Core Funding to WGCI for the implementation of the Program, in the total amount of INR 1,85,00,000 (Indian Rupees One Crore Eighty-Five Lakhs Only) for the Initial Term, to be released in annual installments as follows:

(a) First installment: INR 62,00,000 (Sixty-Two Lakhs Only) upon execution of this Agreement;

(b) Second installment: INR 61,50,000 (Sixty-One Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) upon approval of the Year 2 Annual Work Plan and Budget;

(c) Third installment: INR 61,50,000 (Sixty-One Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) upon approval of the Year 3 Annual Work Plan and Budget.

4.2 WGCI shall provide a Matching Contribution in the form of staff time, office space, and existing field infrastructure, valued at not less than INR 45,00,000 (Forty-Five Lakhs Only) over the Initial Term.

4.3 All funds provided under this Agreement shall be maintained in a separate designated bank account, and shall be utilized solely for the purposes of the Program.

4.4 WGCI shall submit to WTI:

(a) Quarterly financial statements within 30 days of the end of each quarter;

(b) An annual audited statement of accounts within 90 days of the end of each financial year.

4.5 Any unutilized funds at the end of the Term shall be returned to WTI within 60 days, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

**ARTICLE 5: GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT**

5.1 The Parties shall constitute a Steering Committee comprising four (4) members: two nominated by WGCI and two nominated by WTI.

5.2 The Steering Committee shall meet at least once every six (6) months, alternately at the Field Office and at WTI's Noida office, to review program progress, approve work plans, and address any implementation issues.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants contained herein, the Parties agree as follows:

**ARTICLE 1: AMENDMENTS TO THE ORIGINAL AGREEMENT**

1.1 **Extension of Term.** Clause 2.1 of the Original Agreement is hereby amended to extend the Initial Term from three (3) years to four (4) years. The Term shall now commence on 01 April 2019 and end on 31 March 2023, unless terminated earlier in accordance with the Original Agreement.

**ARTICLE 2: UNCHANGED TERMS**

**ARTICLE 3: EFFECTIVE DATE AND EXECUTION**

Sub: Research Permit – Extension of Validity and Revised Conditions – Reg.

Ref: 1. This Office Permit No. KFD/2024/118 dated 05.04.2024
      2. Your application No. CES/2024/118/EXT dated 20.05.2024
      3. Report of the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Mudumalai Division, dated 10.06.2024

With reference to the above, permission granted vide Permit No. KFD/2024/118 dated 05.04.2024 to conduct research titled "Ecology and Behaviour of the Indian Giant Squirrel (Ratufa indica) in the Mudumalai landscape" is hereby extended for a period of six (6) months i.e., up to 04.10.2025, subject to the following revised conditions and the conditions already stipulated in the original permit, insofar as they are not inconsistent with this extension.

2. The research team shall confine their study to the following notified areas:

| Sl. No. | Area | Extent (sq. km) | Remarks |
|---------|------|-----------------|---------|
| 1 | Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) | 688 | KFD official data states Mudumalai TR's area_sq_km is 688 square kilometers. Record status: current. This is the current notified extent as per the latest records. |
| 2 | Sigur Reserve Forest | 94.2 | Adjoining MTR, north-eastern side |
| 3 | Nilgiri North Forest Division (non-notified portions) | 120.5 | Only for movement between study sites |

3. The research team shall not enter the core/critical tiger habitat of Mudumalai Tiger Reserve without prior written permission from the Field Director, Mudumalai Tiger Reserve. The core area extent is 321 sq. km as per the approved Tiger Conservation Plan (2016).

4. The research team shall carry the original permit and this extension letter during all field visits. The identification cards issued by the Centre for Ecological Studies shall be produced on demand by any Forest Officer.

5. The following additional conditions are imposed:

i. The research team shall not use any radio-collars or other telemetry devices on Indian Giant Squirrels without separate prior approval from the Chief Wildlife Warden.

ii. The research team shall not collect any blood, tissue, or other biological samples from animals without separate permission from the Chief Wildlife Warden.

iii. The research team shall not use playback calls of any bird or mammal species, including those of predators, in the study area.

iv. The research team shall not enter the following areas without separate permission:
   - Theppakadu Elephant Camp premises (except the interpretation centre)
   - Kargudi Elephant Camp premises
   - Any anti-poaching camp or forest department residential area

v. The research team shall not use drones or any other unmanned aerial vehicles in the study area.

vi. The research team shall not conduct any research activity during the period from 15.04.2025 to 15.06.2025 (elephant and tiger breeding season) unless specifically permitted in writing by the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Mudumalai Division.

vii. The research team shall not use any motorised vehicles inside the forest areas, except on designated forest roads and with prior permission of the concerned Range Forest Officer.

viii. The research team shall not carry out any research activity in the following areas notified as elephant corridors:
    - Bhavani Sagar – Moyar Corridor
    - Singara – Masinagudi Corridor
    - Theppakadu – Mavanallah Corridor

ix. The research team shall not publish any photographs or videos of forest department staff, camps, or infrastructure without prior written permission.

x. The research team shall not share the GPS coordinates of any den sites, nest sites, or other sensitive locations of wildlife with any person or organisation outside the research team.
